Glyph $00 in the loaded eight-page character source: its eight top-to-bottom row bytes are $00, $00, $00, $00, $00, $00, $00, $00. The captured map refers to it through $00/quadrant 0, $00/quadrant 1, $00/quadrant 2, $00/quadrant 3, $03/quadrant 0, $03/quadrant 1 and 16 more tile/quadrant combinations, using the four quadrant tables at $81CF–$84CF. $717C copies these bytes to $D000 in the character set. The entry was reached during the bounded 200-frame capture and monitor collection. The conditions are tested with controlled inputs; this does not establish a natural route to them.

Load 7 trigger record 1 of 1: initial bytes $09, $05, $01, $01, $2A, $5C. $7979 copies the fields to the column, row, remaining-count, argument and callback arrays; the initial callback address is $5C2A. $48BF compares the stored column and row with the view tile, checks and decrements the count, then dispatches through the callback. Other code can change the stored count.

Load 7 stage object record 1 of 1: initial bytes $40, $0A, $02, $01, $FF, $FF, $62, $91, $B4, $91, $3F, $07, $11, $12, $13, $14. $4655 copies the first 12 fields to per-record arrays and the final four to $7D–$80, then calls $46D6. That map updater can replace those four bytes according to the fourth field and world mode before writing cells. The captured record does not establish that ordinary play reaches its later behavior. Initial selector $02 corresponds to reconstructed screen 11 when field 4 reaches the resource call at $47F5; that forced reconstruction does not establish this record’s ordinary-play reachability.
